The security fixes section changes server-side authorization/validation logic (e.g. "fix(server): require upload access for checksum duplicate check", "fix(server): do not expose album members to shared link viewers") but these are enforcement tightenings, not config-breaking changes.

Per the rc.3 notes carried into this final release's lineage: *"Set `MACHINE_LEARNING_MODEL_REVISION=v2` to take full advantage of the memory usage and performance improvements in this release."* This is not referenced anywhere in the current `.env.example` or compose file for the `immich-machine-learning` service. It is not marked required, but the host is missing the knob needed to get the stated performance benefit of this upgrade.
- No renamed or removed variables found in the notes for this range.

## Upstream changes 8.9.1 -> 9.0.0

**Verdict:** DO NOT APPLY UNATTENDED — this is a major version carrying multiple breaking API/auth changes, a required MongoDB version the compose file does not pin, and an automatic data migration; it needs a deliberate, supervised upgrade.

The release notes state: "MongoDB: `8.0`" as the required engine version for 9.0.0. The compose file pins `mongo:7.0@sha256:...` via `ROCKETCHAT_MONGODB_IMAGE_VERSION:-7.0`. This mismatch alone forces the verdict: the application would run against a database major version its own release notes do not list.

### Breaking changes
- MongoDB engine requirement raised to `8.0` (baseline 8.9.1 already required `8.0` too — see "Data and dependencies" below for what's actually new vs already true). What's new here is nothing further on this axis; the 7.0 pin is already wrong at the current version, not newly broken by this upgrade (see verdict note).
- "Stopped transpiling webhook integration scripts with Babel. Scripts now run as-is inside `isolated-vm`... Class method bodies are now in strict mode" — custom webhook integration scripts using sloppy-mode patterns (implicit globals, `arguments.callee`, octal literals, duplicate params) will break.
- "the `phone` user field is replaced by the `phones` array... existing numbers are migrated automatically on upgrade" — any integration reading/writing the old `phone` field breaks.
- "Removes the deprecated `query` and `fields` REST API parameters, along with the `ALLOW_UNSAFE_QUERY_AND_FIELDS_API_PARAMS` environment variable" — if this variable is set anywhere in a custom `.env` override, it will have no effect and dependent integrations will get `400 error-invalid-params`.
- "Changes the default value of the `Omnichannel enabled` setting (`Livechat_enabled`) to `false`... Existing workspaces keep their current value on upgrade" — no action for an existing deployment, but worth knowing.
- "Removes the 'Allow Anonymous Write' setting... The `anonymous` role is removed... any existing users holding the `anonymous` role are deactivated and logged out."
- "Removes the Atlassian Crowd integration... Users previously provisioned through Crowd keep their accounts... but must sign in through another authentication method."
- "Removes the deprecated `DELETE /v1/canned-responses` endpoint" (body-based); use `DELETE /v1/canned-responses/:_id`.
- "Removes the built-in Gravatar integration" — default avatar behavior changes for new/renamed users.
- "Renames the user `freeSwitchExtension` attribute to `sipExtension`" — any REST integration using the old field name breaks.
- "REST API status codes for authentication and authorization failures now follow their meaning" — 401/403 responses change shape and code; any client/integration parsing `error-invalid-user`, `error-not-authorized`, or status/message fields will need updating.
- "the REST refusals that the API error switch maps answer **403** with one body shape" — same category, broad API client impact.
- "Removed 157 Meteor (DDP) methods" — any external DDP/SDK client calling these by name gets `404`.
- **"Makes LDAP and SAML authentication Premium features. Breaking: workspaces without a Premium plan that includes the `ldap-enterprise` or `saml-enterprise` module lose LDAP and SAML login on upgrade to 9.0.0. Keep a Premium license or an admin account that signs in another way before upgrading."** — critical for any self-hosted deployment using LDAP/SAML without an Enterprise license.
- "Makes Custom OAuth authentication a Premium feature, gated by the `oauth-enterprise` license module. On workspaces without it, the enable setting of every Custom OAuth service falls back to `false`."
- "Removes the built-in Drupal, Facebook, GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn, Meteor, Twitter, WordPress and Dolphin OAuth login providers."
- "Removes the legacy Meteor OAuth login flow and the `Accounts_OAuth_Use_Modern_Flow` setting" plus removal of `Accounts_OAuth_Proxy_host`/`Accounts_OAuth_Proxy_services`.
- "The web client no longer ships Meteor's client packages... Code that runs in the page and relies on those packages stops working, in particular the custom scripts of `Custom_Script_On_Logout`, `Custom_Script_Logged_Out` and `Custom_Script_Logged_In`" — affects any admin-configured custom scripts.
- "Removes the WebDAV integration."
- "Removes `/ufs` legacy endpoint for downloading files."

### Variables
- `ALLOW_UNSAFE_QUERY_AND_FIELDS_API_PARAMS` — removed; has no effect if set.
- `MESSAGE_MAX_PARSE_LENGTH` default changes from `0` to `10000`: "Changes the default value of the `MESSAGE_MAX_PARSE_LENGTH` environment variable from `0` (no limit) to `10000` characters... Workspaces using the default `Message_MaxAllowedSize` (5000) are not affected." Not set in this compose file or .env.example, so the new default applies unless an operator previously relied on unlimited parsing.
- `Push_UseLegacy`, `Push_gcm_project_number`, `Push_gcm_api_key` — removed (settings, not compose/.env variables here; no match in this template).
- None of the removed/renamed settings (`CROWD_*`, `FEDERATION_*`, `Accounts_OAuth_*`, `Push_gcm_*`) appear in this compose file's `environment:` block or in `.env.example`, so no edit to these two files is required.

### Data and dependencies
- **Already true at 8.9.1 (not introduced by this upgrade):** MongoDB `8.0` was already the stated engine requirement in the 8.9.1 baseline notes. The compose file pins `mongo:7.0`, so this gap predates the upgrade — but it still triggers the DO NOT APPLY UNATTENDED verdict per the rule that an unlisted engine version is a stop condition regardless of when the gap was introduced.
- Irreversible/automatic migrations on upgrade, per the notes: `phone` → `phones` array; `freeSwitchExtension` → `sipExtension`; stale `Drafts` sidebar group removal; deletion of `anonymous` role/setting, Crowd settings, legacy federation settings, `Use_RC_SDK` setting, WebDAV settings, GCM push settings.
- Federated room version for newly created rooms changes from 10 to 11 (existing rooms unaffected) — informational, no action.
- No change to container ports, volumes, user, entrypoint, command, or healthcheck — confirmed identical between the two image builds per the registry comparison.

### Before applying
- Confirm whether LDAP or SAML login is in use and whether a Premium/Enterprise license with the `ldap-enterprise` or `saml-enterprise` module is active. If not, **do not upgrade** until either a Premium license is obtained or a non-LDAP/SAML admin account is confirmed working — the notes are explicit: "Keep a Premium license or an admin account that signs in another way before upgrading."
- Resolve the MongoDB version gap before or as part of this upgrade: plan a controlled upgrade path from the currently pinned `mongo:7.0` to `8.0`, including a replica-set-aware rolling upgrade and a verified backup, since this template runs MongoDB as a single-member replica set (`rs0`) with backups via `mongodump`.
- Take a full backup (the `backups` service already runs `mongodump` on schedule — trigger an out-of-band run and verify the archive) before upgrading the Rocket.Chat image, since several changes delete settings/roles/data from the database on upgrade and are not reversible by downgrading the image alone.
- Audit any custom webhook integration scripts for sloppy-mode JavaScript patterns (implicit globals, `arguments.callee`, octal literals, duplicate parameters) — these will throw under the new strict-mode execution.
- Audit any external DDP/SDK clients and REST API integrations for use of the 157 removed DDP methods, the removed `query`/`fields` REST parameters, the old `phone`/`freeSwitchExtension` fields, and the old `DELETE /v1/canned-responses` body-based call.
- Review any admin-configured `Custom_Script_On_Logout` / `Custom_Script_Logged_Out` / `Custom_Script_Logged_In` settings for reliance on Meteor client globals (`Meteor.userId()`, `Tracker`, etc.) — these must be rewritten to read `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` and call the REST API.
- After upgrade, re-check authentication for any users previously provisioned through Crowd or a removed OAuth provider (Drupal, Facebook, GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn, Meteor, Twitter, WordPress, Dolphin) — they must switch to a remaining method.
- Bump `ROCKETCHAT_MONGODB_IMAGE_VERSION`/pin in the compose file's `x-images` block once the MongoDB upgrade path is executed; this is a template maintenance action, not a `.env` edit.

### Notes read
- 9.0.0 (2026-11-10) — full release notes as supplied.
- 8.9.1 (2026-11-06) — read only as the stated baseline, to separate already-true requirements from changes introduced by this range.
